surface_mechanism_description: The as-deposited MgO film is reactive to atmospheric moisture and carbon dioxide, with Mg–OH groups turning into MgO upon annealing. The interfacial reaction between MgO and Si substrates leads to the formation of magnesium silicate and silicides.
evidence: XPS results indicate that the as-deposited MgO film is quite reactive to the atmospheric moisture and carbon dioxide and has a sharp interface with the substrate. The spectra of samples annealed at 600°C show that the Mg–OH groups have been turned into MgO. RTA also induces the formation of magnesium silicate, whose content increases with increasing annealing temperature.
